- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 3% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% of spike magnitude.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is trending upward; apply a +0.5 to +1.5 price point bias to forecast.
- Model overestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is trending downward; apply -0.5 to -1.5 price point bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.4 → -0.2 → +0.6), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not just history.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 0.5–1.0 point correction toward historical mean or 30-day average.
